runs.answer: Partial answer only. I could not verify whether the bridge has since reopened to traffic.

runs.title: Danny Kelly: confirm the news and the tributes
runs.prompt: Danny Kelly, the former NME/Q editor and long-time BBC and talkSPORT football broadcaster, is reported to have died at age 69. Find out: (1) confirm the date and reported cause of death from a reputable non-paywalled source; (2) what he was known for in journalism and broadcasting; and (3) one or two notable tributes from people he worked with. Start from the BBC and Guardian pages and follow links.
runs.answer: Danny Kelly died on Tuesday 10 November 2026 (announced on talkSPORT the following day, 11 November), aged 69, while being treated for oesophageal cancer — he had told talkSPORT viewers on 18 March 2026 that he had been diagnosed and was stepping back. He was NME editor from the late 1980s to 1992 and later editor of Q (named British magazine editor of the year), co-launched Football365 and The Times' football podcast The Game, co-presented BBC radio shows with Danny Baker in the 1990s, had a sports show on BBC London before joining talkSPORT in 2007 for nearly 20 years, and hosted the Spurs podcast The View From The Lane as a lifelong Tottenham fan. Tributes included Danny Baker calling him "my great friend, supreme broadcaster and funniest man I ever knew", former NME editor Conor McNicholas saying "The NME wouldn't be the NME without Danny", the Manic Street Preachers' Nicky Wire praising "a brilliant broadcaster-writer-ideas factory", and talkSPORT calling him "a cherished part" of the station and "a broadcasting titan". Note: the BBC Sport piece said "throat cancer", but the Guardian, NME and other reports say oesophageal cancer, which appears to be correct.

runs.answer: Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal at Camp Nou (12 Nov 2026), a UWCL league-phase matchday 4 game. There is no return leg in this format: Arsenal's next Champions League fixture is at home to Lyon at Meadow Park on Thursday 19 November 2026, with a WSL trip to London City Lionesses in between on Sunday.

runs.prompt: U2 is releasing a song called 'Torn' that features Dolly Parton's final recorded vocals, done as a posthumous duet with Bono, reportedly out 13 November 2026. runs.answer: Confirmed: 'Torn', U2's posthumous duet with Dolly Parton, came out on Friday 13 November 2026 as the closing track of U2's 16th studio album, 'Carnaval De Luz' (produced by Jacknife Lee, 12 songs, with Rosalía also guesting on 'The Mirror Maker') — the album's release date is the same day, i.e. the song arrived as the album dropped (ABC, publishing on 13 Nov 2026, writes "Released today"; NME's September announcement and U2's own site both give 13 November). "Final recording" means it is the last vocal performance of her career, not an archival outtake: Parton recorded her vocal in Nashville in June 2026 — under three months before she died on 25 August 2026, aged 80, after a brief battle with cancer — and Bono told Rolling Stone she "got out of her bed to sing this song," adding "I can't even listen to it now." She co-wrote 'Torn' (U2 and Snow Patrol's Johnny McDaid reworked her original lyric into a family divided by politics) and was able to hear and approve the final mix before her death; two further versions, by Kent Wells and T Bone Burnett, were also released on 13 November. One small discrepancy to note: Rolling Stone-derived coverage (NME, Hot Press) says "just two months

runs.prompt: Robert Eggers' new werewolf horror film 'Werwulf' (starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson) has been given an R rating by the MPA for disturbing violence, gore, sexual assault and graphic nudity, ahead of a Christmas 2026 release. Your job is to choose the single clearest, most complete source that states the rating and the official MPA reasons verbatim, plus the release date, and that loads in full from a plain GET request. runs.answer: Best source: Dread Central's "Robert Eggers' 'Werwulf' Rated R for Gore, Sexual Assault and Graphic Nudity" (Brad Miska, Nov 10, 2026) — it loads in full via a plain GET and states, verbatim, that Werwulf is rated R for "strong bloody/disturbing violent content, gore, sexual assault, graphic nudity and strong sexual content," and that Focus Features opens the film in theaters December 25, 2026 (with 35mm tickets already on sale). It's the clearest single source: rating, full official descriptor string in quotes, cast/director context and release date all on one readable page, with no bot wall or JavaScript gating.

runs.title: Stunt: pry Werwulf's R-rating from Variety
runs.prompt: Variety has covered Robert Eggers' 'Werwulf' (the Aaron Taylor-Johnson werewolf film) including its trailer and likely its MPA R rating for disturbing violence, gore, sexual assault and graphic nudity. Your task: go to Variety and retrieve the specifics of the film's R rating and release date from Variety's own coverage. Start on the Variety film news page for Werwulf and try to load the article in full. Document exactly what you can and cannot read — if a bot wall, paywall or JavaScript-only page stops you, describe precisely where it failed. The wall is the story.
runs.answer: Variety's Werwulf coverage was fully readable — no paywall or bot wall on Variety itself — but Variety has published NO article about the film's MPA rating. The only hard fact I could pull is the release date: "Werwulf hits theaters on Dec. 25" (Christmas Day 2026), from Jordan Moreau's Apr. 15, 2026 CinemaCon story, which also notes the first-look trailer showed a nude Aaron Taylor-Johnson transforming into the werewolf, mauled corpses and desecrated graves. Variety's Werwulf tag/RSS feed lists exactly five items (Jan 2025 release-date news, Jul 2025 casting, the Apr 2026 CinemaCon trailer story, a Jun 2026 trailer story, and an Oscar cinematography predictions piece) — none about an R rating or its descriptors. The June 2026 trailer story is the last place a rating note could hide, but I hit my visit limit before reading its body. The specific "R for disturbing violence, gore, sexual assault and graphic nudity" wording is therefore unverified by Variety sources and should not be attributed to them without checking that article.
